title: Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)
summary: Spot a low, treat it with the 15-15 rule, and know when it is a severe low that needs glucagon and 911.

sources.title: CDC - Treatment of Low Blood Sugar (Hypoglycemia)
American Diabetes Association - Signs, Symptoms, and Treatment for Hypoglycemia

Dexcom G7 User Guide (treatment decisions and safety information)

blocks.text: **Severe low:** the person is passed out, having a seizure, confused to the point of not helping themselves, or cannot swallow safely. Do NOT put food or drink in their mouth. Give **glucagon** (see the glucagon guide) and call **911** right after. If there is no glucagon, or nobody knows how to use it, call **911 immediately**. If they are unconscious, roll them onto their side.

blocks.alt: Severe low blood sugar: if the person is unconscious, roll them onto their side. The drawing shows a person lying on their back, an arrow marked roll, and the person lying on their side. Put no food or drink in their mouth. Give glucagon, then call 911. If there is no glucagon, or nobody knows how to use it, call 911 immediately.
blocks.caption: If the person is unconscious, roll them onto their side.

items: Shaky, nervous or anxious; sweaty, chills, clammy
Fast heartbeat, dizzy or lightheaded, hungry, nauseated
Irritable, confused, hard to think or speak clearly
Pale, sleepy, weak, blurred vision, headache, clumsy
Tingling or numb lips, tongue or cheeks
At night: nightmares, crying out, soaked sheets, waking up tired or confused
Some people feel nothing at all (hypoglycemia unawareness), so do not rely on symptoms alone

blocks.text: A low is **below 70 mg/dL**. **Below 55 mg/dL** is a severely low reading. If you cannot check but you have symptoms, treat it as a low.
Mild or moderate low: the 15-15 rule

blocks.alt: Low blood sugar, the 15-15 rule. A low is below 70 mg/dL, and below 55 mg/dL is severely low. 1: check with your meter. 2: eat or drink 15 grams of fast-acting carbohydrate. 3: wait 15 minutes. 4: check again. If still below 70, repeat. If above 70 and the next meal is not soon, eat a snack with protein and carbs, such as cheese and crackers. If the person is passed out, having a seizure or cannot swallow, put no food or drink in their mouth, give glucagon and then call 911, and if there is no glucagon call 911 now.
blocks.caption: The 15-15 rule as a loop.

items: Check with your meter. If your CGM number does not match how you feel, trust the meter and your symptoms.
Eat or drink **15 grams** of fast-acting carbohydrate (see the table below). NIDDK gives a range of 15 to 20 grams, so use the amount your care team has told you.
Still below 70 mg/dL, or your CGM is not trending up? Take another 15 grams and wait 15 minutes again. Repeat until you are back above 70.
Once you are above 70, if your next meal is not soon, eat a snack with protein and carbs, such as cheese and crackers, so you do not drop again.

rows: Fruit juice or regular (not diet) soda
The number of tablets on the package that equals 15 g (CDC says 3 to 4 tablets, but brands differ)
Usually 1 tube; check the label for 15 g
Check the label for the amount that equals 15 g

blocks.text: Skip chocolate and peanut butter for treating a low. The fat and protein slow down the sugar. Diet soda has no sugar and does not work.

items: Glucagon is the best treatment for a severe low. It comes as a nasal powder, a ready-to-use pen or syringe, or a kit you mix.
Use it if the 15-15 rule is not working, the person cannot safely swallow, they are confused or about to pass out, or they are unconscious.
Call 911 right after giving it, even if the person wakes up.
Once they are awake and can swallow, give a fast sugar, then a snack with protein and carbs, and tell their doctor.
If glucagon is missing or expired, talk to your doctor soon about a replacement, preferably a ready-to-use form.

blocks.text: Step-by-step use for each product is in the glucagon guide.

items: Use your meter instead of the CGM when the CGM shows no number or no arrow, or when your symptoms do not match the reading. Never ignore symptoms of a low.
Keep fast carbs in every bag, car and bedside table, and make sure the people you live with know where the glucagon is.

blocks.text: Wear a medical ID so others know you have diabetes. Check the glucagon expiration date regularly. Frequent lows are worth a call to your diabetes team, because repeated lows can make you stop feeling the early warning signs.
